_meta.description: LLM-generated Critics' Take summaries for shows (concise 1-2 sentence summary, max 280 chars)
_meta.updatePolicy: Regenerate weekly if 3+ new reviews added to any show

two-strangers-bway-2025.text: This charming British import rom-com earns mostly warm reviews for its modest sincerity and winning leads, though critics split on whether its lightweight, formulaic story offers enough substance beyond sweetness.

maybe-happy-ending-2024.text: Critics hail this charming Korean import about obsolete robots falling in love as one of Broadway's most original musicals in years, praising its emotional depth, visual innovation, and intimate storytelling that's both silly and surprisingly moving.

the-outsiders-2024.text: Critics are mixed on this Hinton adaptation, praising its thrilling choreography and energetic young cast while finding the familiar story competent but forgettable. The folk-country score and visceral staging earn acclaim, though some see it as derivative.

hells-kitchen-2024.text: Critics praise Hell's Kitchen for powerhouse vocals and electrifying choreography that elevate Alicia Keys' catalog, though many find the coming-of-age story formulaic and thin.

operation-mincemeat-2025.text: This scrappy British musical about a WWII deception operation charms critics with its clever humor and energetic five-person cast, though some find its frenetic style exhausting and too clever by half.

oh-mary-2024.text: Critics hail Cole Escola's irreverent Mary Todd Lincoln comedy as dizzyingly, gut-bustingly funny—a campy, absurdist farce that delivers some of Broadway's biggest laughs with vulgar wit and theatrical anarchy, though a few find it too silly.

the-great-gatsby-2024.text: Critics find this lavish Gatsby musical visually dazzling but emotionally hollow, with spectacular production design that can't compensate for a shallow book that misses Fitzgerald's themes and reduces the story to standard romance.

bug-2026.text: Critics praise this intense psychological thriller for Coon's raw, fearless performance and its timely resonance with conspiracy culture, though some find Cromer's direction too leisurely and the '90s play feels minor in Letts's canon.

hamilton-2015.text: Critics hail "Hamilton" as a groundbreaking masterpiece, praising Lin-Manuel Miranda's audacious hip-hop score, brilliant writing, and innovative storytelling that makes American history electrifying and accessible for modern audiences.

the-lion-king-1997.text: Critics hail Julie Taymor's staging as a theatrical marvel, with groundbreaking puppetry and visual spectacle that transcends the Disney film. While universally praised for its imaginative artistry, some find the storytelling less engaging than the stunning visuals.

chicago-1996.text: Critics praise this stripped-down revival as wildly entertaining and surprisingly vital, with sharp performances and Fosse-style choreography keeping the show fresh despite its long run and frequent cast changes.

moulin-rouge-2019.text: Critics are dazzled by the lavish spectacle and stunning production design but divided on substance, with some finding it a thrilling sensory overload and others dismissing it as excessive style over emotional depth.

aladdin-2014.text: Critics find Disney's "Aladdin" a visually dazzling, family-friendly spectacle elevated by James Monroe Iglehart's scene-stealing Genie, though many note it lacks the magic of the original film and relies heavily on familiar Disney formula.

hadestown-2019.text: Critics hail Hadestown as a stunning, original folk opera with gorgeous music and visionary staging, though some find its story emotionally distant. Mitchell's score and Chavkin's direction earn widespread praise for reimagining Greek myth with contemporary resonance.

mj-2022.text: Critics praise the electrifying choreography and performances in this Michael Jackson musical, but fault the estate-sanctioned production for glossing over controversies and delivering hagiography over honest biography.

six-2021.text: Critics embrace this high-energy pop concert musical about Henry VIII's wives as joyous feminist fun, though some question whether it's more concert than theater. The 80-minute show dazzles with catchy songs and powerhouse performances.

book-of-mormon-2011.text: Critics hail this irreverent satire from the South Park creators as hilariously offensive yet surprisingly sweet, with sharp wit that skewers religion and Broadway conventions while delivering genuine heart.

and-juliet-2022.text: Critics find this Max Martin jukebox musical reimagining Juliet's survival a silly but infectious crowd-pleaser, with energetic performances and pop hits winning over most reviewers despite its unsubtle feminism and lightweight book.

oedipus-2025.text: Robert Icke's sleek modern adaptation transforms Sophocles into a gripping political thriller, powered by stellar performances from Mark Strong and Lesley Manville, though some critics find it overly polished at the expense of emotional catharsis.

harry-potter-2021.text: Critics praise the spectacular stagecraft and magical illusions as breathtaking, calling it a theatrical marvel that brings Rowling's world vividly to life. Some find the story feels like expensive fan fiction, but most agree it's an enchanting, emotionally resonant experience.

mamma-mia-2025.text: Critics find this ABBA jukebox musical a silly, feather-light guilty pleasure—preposterous plot and flimsy production aside, those irresistibly catchy disco hits work happy magic on audiences, even if the show barely qualifies as serious theater.

stranger-things-2024.text: Critics praise the spectacle and technical wizardry but find the three-hour prequel narratively thin, with most agreeing it's a visually stunning theme park experience that prioritizes effects over storytelling depth.

cabaret-2024.text: Critics are divided on this immersive revival: while the transformed theater space and Redmayne's performance impress, many find the elaborate preshow gimmickry overshadows the show's darker themes and moral urgency.

stereophonic-2024.text: Critics hail Adjmi's hyper-naturalistic drama as a masterwork, praising its authentic depiction of the creative process and stunning technical design. The three-hour studio-set play earns near-universal acclaim for its immersive storytelling.

water-for-elephants-2024.text: Critics praise the spectacular circus acrobatics and ensemble work, but find the story formulaic and the score unmemorable. The staging dazzles even when the melodramatic romance doesn't, making for impressive spectacle over substance.

suffs-2024.text: Critics praise Shaina Taub's ambitious, tuneful musical about the suffrage movement as entertaining and well-performed, though some find it more educational than dramatically compelling, occasionally feeling like a civics lesson set to music.

the-notebook-2024.text: Critics are mixed on this romantic musical adaptation, finding it emotionally effective for fans but often too sentimental. The staging and performances earn praise, though the score lacks standout numbers.

marjorie-prime-2025.text: Critics praise this timely AI drama's sharp performances, especially 96-year-old June Squibb's masterful turn, though some find Harrison's premise feels less fresh a decade later. The production resonates more deeply in today's AI-saturated world.

liberation-2025.text: Critics hail Bess Wohl's ambitious feminist drama as the year's best play, praising its intricate structure, superb ensemble cast, and timely exploration of 1970s consciousness-raising groups that resonates powerfully today.

boop-2025.text: Critics praise Jasmine Amy Rogers' sensational Broadway debut in this polished, old-fashioned crowd-pleaser, though some question why it exists. The glittery production offers escapist fun, but reviews split on its thin story.

queen-versailles-2025.text: Critics are divided on this excess-themed musical, with Chenoweth's performance widely praised but the show itself criticized for tonal confusion—unable to decide whether to satirize or celebrate its billionaire protagonist's materialism.

death-becomes-her-2024.text: Critics praise this campy musical adaptation as a significant improvement over the 1992 film, with Megan Hilty and Jennifer Simard delivering stellar comic performances in a raucously entertaining crowd-pleaser.

buena-vista-social-club-2025.text: Critics praise the intoxicating Cuban music and exuberant choreography that transport audiences to Havana, though most agree the thin, clichéd book holds back an otherwise joyful and visually stunning celebration.

ragtime-2025.text: Critics praise this stirring revival as powerfully resonant for today, with a glorious cast and soaring score compensating for its stripped-down staging, though some find it overlong or too earnest.

chess-2025.text: Mixed reviews greet this Broadway revival of the famously troubled Cold War musical. Critics praise the powerhouse vocals and infectious ABBA score, but find the book still convoluted despite rewrites that lean into camp over coherence.

just-in-time-2025.text: Jonathan Groff dazzles in this slick but formulaic Bobby Darin bio-musical that doesn't reinvent the jukebox genre but thrives on its star's charisma and the intimate nightclub staging at Circle in the Square.

the-roommate-2024.text: LuPone and Farrow's star power elevates Silverman's slight, uneven odd-couple comedy about mismatched roommates. Critics praise the leads' magnetic chemistry and performances, though most find the script thin and predictable.

our-town-2024.text: Critics find Kenny Leon's revival of Wilder's classic mostly effective and emotionally resonant, with strong praise for Jim Parsons and its timeless themes, though some feel it lacks the innovation to fully distinguish itself from past productions.

back-to-the-future-2023.text: Critics find this faithful film adaptation a visually dazzling spectacle with a flying DeLorean that wows audiences, but note a forgettable score and overly safe storytelling that prioritizes nostalgia over theatrical innovation.

real-women-have-curves-2025.text: Critics embrace this crowd-pleasing musical about Latina garment workers as funny, heartfelt, and timely, praising its body-positive anthem and winning ensemble, though some find it leans sentimental over its darker immigration themes.

redwood-2025.text: Critics find Menzel's powerful vocals elevate a dramatically thin, overly earnest musical about grief, with spectacular scenic/video design overshadowing a familiar, undercooked story that struggles to find emotional depth.

days-of-wine-and-roses-2024.text: O'Hara and d'Arcy James deliver superb performances in this challenging musical adaptation, elevated by Guettel's distinctive score, though critics debate whether the dark subject matter of alcoholism suits the musical form.

harmony-2023.text: Critics find Manilow's long-gestating musical about the Comedian Harmonists earnest and timely, with beautiful vocals and a moving story, but many note structural flaws, uneven pacing, and a conventional approach that doesn't fully soar.

here-lies-love-2023.text: Critics praise the immersive disco staging and historic all-Filipino cast, though some question whether the dazzling spectacle overshadows the dark political history at its core.

how-to-dance-in-ohio-2023.text: Critics find this groundbreaking musical featuring autistic actors heartwarming and well-intentioned, but note it struggles with multiple storylines and uneven execution. The cast earns universal praise for their authenticity and charm.

illinoise-2024.text: Justin Peck's dance-theater hybrid adaptation of Sufjan Stevens' concept album earns mostly strong reviews for its ambitious, emotionally expressive choreography, though some critics question the narrative coherence of this genre-defying work.

lempicka-2024.text: Critics find "Lempicka" visually striking but narratively muddled, with an ambitious bio-musical about the Art Deco painter hampered by conventional storytelling and uneven execution despite strong design elements.

once-upon-a-one-more-time-2023.text: Critics are divided on this Britney Spears jukebox musical about feminist fairy tale princesses. Some praise its high-energy fun and creative choreography, while others dismiss it as derivative and heavy-handed, comparing it unfavorably to similar shows.

heart-of-rock-and-roll-2024.text: This Huey Lewis jukebox musical earns mostly positive reviews for its unpretentious fun and catchy '80s nostalgia, though critics note the book is formulaic. It's a pleasant surprise that doesn't take itself too seriously.

gutenberg-2023.text: Critics are mixed on this silly meta-musical parody, praising the comic chemistry of stars Josh Gad and Andrew Rannells while finding the thin premise and repetitive jokes wear thin over two hours.

merrily-we-roll-along-2023.text: Maria Friedman's revival transforms Sondheim's notorious 1981 flop into a triumphant Broadway hit. Critics hail the production as revelatory, with particular praise for the stellar trio of Groff, Radcliffe, and Mendez.

spamalot-2023.text: Critics find this "Spamalot" revival as hilariously silly as ever, with a perfectly cast ensemble delivering the Monty Python absurdity. Some jokes feel dated, but the show's scrappy, irreverent spirit offers much-needed comic relief.

the-whos-tommy-2024.text: This electrifying revival delivers a visceral sonic assault and spectacular visuals that thrill fans, though some critics find the relentless sensory overload obscures the story's emotional depth.

the-wiz-2024.text: Critics are mixed on this "Wiz" revival, praising its joyful energy and spectacular design but criticizing uneven direction and choices that don't capture the original's magic.

grey-house-2023.text: Critics are mixed on this Broadway horror play, praising its atmospheric stagecraft and performances (especially Metcalf) but faulting its reliance on familiar tropes and uneven scares that don't always land.

i-need-that-2023.text: DeVito charms in this thin, sitcom-like comedy about hoarding, but critics find Rebeck's play repetitive and dramatically inert. The star's performance earns praise, yet the slight material and underdeveloped characters leave most reviewers wanting more substance.

jajas-african-hair-braiding-2023.text: Critics praise Bioh's vibrant ensemble comedy set in a Harlem braiding salon for its sparkling cast, exuberant humor, and stunning design, though some find its late tonal shift and effort to cover immigration issues dilutes the workplace comedy's focus.

just-for-us-2023.text: Critics hail Edelman's solo show about infiltrating a white nationalist meeting as hilarious and sharply crafted, praising his rapid-fire wit and ability to balance uproarious comedy with thoughtful commentary on identity and antisemitism.

mary-jane-2024.text: Critics praise Herzog's understated, compassionate play and McAdams' powerhouse Broadway debut as a mother caring for her severely ill son, though some find the drama too schematic or emotionally exhausting.

mother-play-2024.text: Vogel's semi-autobiographical family drama earns mixed-positive reviews, with critics praising Lange's commanding performance and inventive staging but finding the play itself uneven and emotionally underpowered compared to its star power.

patriots-2024.text: Critics find Peter Morgan's Putin-rise drama gripping but uneven, with Michael Stuhlbarg's powerhouse performance as oligarch Boris Berezovsky earning widespread praise while the play itself draws mixed reactions for lacking deeper insight.

prayer-for-the-french-republic-2024.text: Harmon's ambitious three-hour drama about a French Jewish family grappling with antisemitism across generations earns praise for its timeliness and strong ensemble, though some critics find it overstuffed and struggling under the weight of its sprawling structure.

the-cottage-2023.text: Critics are divided on this Noël Coward-inspired farce, with some finding it a delightful summer romp and others dismissing it as crude and derivative. The cast earns praise, but the comedy's reliance on lowbrow humor and lack of sophistication disappoints many.

the-shark-is-broken-2023.text: Critics find this behind-the-scenes look at the troubled "Jaws" shoot amiable and well-acted, but dramatically inert. While the performances and premise charm, most agree the play lacks action and depth, leaving audiences hungry for more bite.

an-enemy-of-the-people-2024.text: Jeremy Strong delivers an intense, compelling performance in Amy Herzog's timely adaptation of Ibsen's classic, though Sam Gold's staging draws mixed reactions—some find it urgent and electrifying, others underwhelming.

appropriate-2023.text: Critics hail this searing family drama as a modern masterpiece with blistering ensemble work led by Sarah Paulson's monumental performance, though some find its larger ambitions don't fully cohere beneath the dysfunction and dark humor.

doubt-2024.text: Shanley's Pulitzer-winning drama remains gripping with powerful performances from Ryan and Schreiber, though critics note the play's ambiguity feels less potent 20 years later as real-world abuse scandals have tipped the scales of doubt.

purlie-victorious-2023.text: Kenny Leon's exuberant revival of Ossie Davis' 1961 satire proves strikingly relevant, with critics praising Leslie Odom Jr.'s performance and the production's ability to skewer racism through raucous comedy that still resonates today.

uncle-vanya-2024.text: Critics are mixed on this starry "Uncle Vanya," praising Steve Carell's melancholic Broadway debut and Lila Neugebauer's direction, but many find the production disjointed and struggling to cohere in the vast Beaumont space.

titanique-2026.text: Critics praise this campy Celine Dion-scored parody of the Titanic film as outrageously funny and joyfully irreverent, skewering jukebox musicals with clever wit. It's pure escapist fun rather than high art, delivering silly, nasty, delicious laughs.

home-2024.text: Kenny Leon's revival of Samm-Art Williams' 1979 play earns warm praise for its poetic storytelling and powerful performances, though some critics find the material dated and the production uneven in its execution.

job-2024.text: Critics find this tense two-hander about a viral-video tech worker holding her therapist at gunpoint to be gripping but gimmicky, with strong performances from Lemmon and Friedman elevating a provocative premise that struggles to sustain its shock value.

once-upon-a-mattress-2024.text: Critics praise Sutton Foster's dazzling comic performance in this charming but bare-bones Encores! transfer, though some find the production more dutiful than inspired. Foster and Michael Urie's chemistry delights, even if the staging feels rushed.

the-hills-of-california-2024.text: Critics praise Butterworth's richly layered family drama and Donnelly's stunning dual performance, though some find the three-hour saga overly familiar. Mendes' direction and atmospheric production values earn acclaim despite debates over narrative depth.

mcneal-2024.text: Robert Downey Jr. delivers a magnetic Broadway debut in Ayad Akhtar's AI-focused drama, but critics find the play itself muddled and dramatically inert, raising intriguing questions about technology and creativity without landing on satisfying answers.

yellow-face-2024.text: Critics praise Hwang's sharp, hilarious meta-theatrical comedy about race and identity as timely and provocative, with Daniel Dae Kim delivering a terrific performance. Some find it messy or self-indulgent, but most laud its wit and relevance.

sunset-boulevard-2024.text: Lloyd's stripped-down, camera-driven revival electrifies with Scherzinger's powerhouse Broadway debut as Norma, though critics split on whether the bold staging enhances or overwhelms Lloyd Webber's melodrama.

left-on-tenth-2024.text: Critics find this memoir adaptation charming but dramatically inert, with Margulies' warm performance praised while the play itself struggles to translate a personal story into compelling theater, often feeling more suited to film or the page.

romeo-juliet-2024.text: Sam Gold's Gen Z-targeted revival draws mixed reactions: fans of stars Kit Connor and Rachel Zegler embrace the energetic, modern aesthetic with Jack Antonoff's music, but many critics find the hyperactive staging gimmicky and patronizing.

a-wonderful-world-the-louis-armstrong-mu.text: James Monroe Iglehart's remarkable performance elevates this jukebox biomusical, but critics find the book overly formulaic and information-heavy, struggling with the familiar challenges of the biographical musical genre.

tammy-faye-2024.text: Critics find "Tammy Faye" tonally confused and unfocused, struggling between camp and compassion. Katie Brayben's powerhouse performance earns praise, but Elton John's score and the production's spectacle can't overcome a messy, uneven narrative.

elf-2024.text: Critics find this holiday revival a cheerful crowd-pleaser elevated by Grey Henson's winning performance as Buddy, though the forgettable score and thin material prevent it from being more than festive, family-friendly fun.

swept-away-2024.text: Critics are divided on this dark Avett Brothers musical about shipwrecked sailors. While the folk-rock score and staging earn praise, many find the grim story sleepy and dramatically unsatisfying, with characters lacking depth.

cult-of-love-2024.text: Critics find Headland's dysfunctional family Christmas drama caustically funny and well-acted, though some feel it's overstuffed with issues. The starry cast and sharp writing earn praise, but the play divides on whether it's compelling or cluttered.

eureka-day-2024.text: Spector's sharp satire of progressive Berkeley parents debating vaccines during a mumps outbreak earns mostly positive reviews for its humor and stellar cast, though some find its both-sides approach uncomfortable or its characters too cartoonish.

gypsy-2024.text: Critics hail McDonald's grounded, deeply moving take on Mama Rose as revelatory, bringing unprecedented emotional depth to the iconic role. Wolfe's revival is widely praised as electric and heartstopping, though a few find it slow-paced.

all-in-comedy-about-love-2024.text: Simon Rich's star-studded staged reading draws mixed reviews, with critics praising its gentle wit and celebrity charm but questioning its value as theater—some call it a cash grab while others find it pleasantly amusing holiday fare.

english-2025.text: Toossi's Pulitzer-winning drama earns widespread praise for its smart, sensitive exploration of language and identity through Iranian students learning English. Critics laud its understated power and moving performances, though some find it slow-moving.

purpose-2025.text: Jacobs-Jenkins delivers another searing family drama with crackling dialogue and powerhouse performances, though its ambitious second act doesn't quite match the brilliant first's sitcom-sharp heights.

othello-2025.text: Critics find this star-powered "Othello" disappointingly underpowered, with Washington and Gyllenhaal's performances unable to overcome Kenny Leon's uninspired direction and lack of a cohesive vision for the production.

the-picture-of-dorian-gray-2025.text: Sarah Snook dazzles in a technically innovative one-woman tour de force, playing 26 characters amid cameras and screens. Critics praise her virtuosic performance, though some find the tech spectacle overshadows emotional depth.

glengarry-glen-ross-2025.text: Critics are divided on this starry revival, with many praising the strong cast (especially Odenkirk) but questioning whether Mamet's play still resonates. The cavernous Palace Theatre and uneven pacing dampen the production's impact.

good-night-and-good-luck-2025.text: Critics find Clooney's Broadway debut timely and handsomely staged by Cromer, but the faithful film adaptation feels overly didactic and static for theater, relying too heavily on screens that undercut the live experience.

the-last-five-years-2025.text: Brown's beloved score shines in its long-awaited Broadway bow, but the production suffers from uneven casting, with Jonas struggling to match Tony winner Warren's powerhouse performance in this intimate two-hander about a failing marriage.

stephen-sondheims-old-friends-2025.text: Critics find this Sondheim revue a lavish, well-performed tribute elevated by Bernadette Peters and talented cast, though some feel the 40-song collection lacks flow and context, making it more a treat for devoted fans than essential theater.

john-proctor-is-the-villain-2025.text: Critics praise this sharp, timely reimagining of "The Crucible" through a #MeToo lens as funny, provocative, and emotionally charged, with standout performances—though some find it heavy-handed and in need of another draft.

floyd-collins-2025.text: Critics praise Guettel's beautiful score and Jordan's powerful performance, but opinions split on whether this chamber piece works in the larger Vivian Beaumont space, with some finding it moving and others feeling it lacks urgency.

pirates-the-penzance-musical-2025.text: Critics largely embrace this jazzy New Orleans reimagining of Gilbert & Sullivan's classic, with David Hyde Pierce earning particular praise, though purists may bristle at the liberties taken with the beloved operetta.

dead-outlaw-2025.text: Critics praise this darkly inventive musical about outlaw Elmer McCurdy's bizarre afterlife as a sideshow corpse. Yazbek and Della Penna's rockabilly score and Cromer's sharp direction elevate a macabre true story into a pointed commentary on American greed.

the-kite-runner-2022.text: Mixed reviews greet this faithful adaptation of Hosseini's bestseller, with critics praising its emotional power and fluid staging but faulting a clunky, overly literal script that relies too heavily on narration over action.

into-the-woods-2022.text: Critics hail this stripped-down revival as a transcendent tribute to Sondheim, praising its exceptional cast, emotional directness, and musical perfection. The pared-back staging lets the material shine, creating an enchanting production both fresh and faithful.

leopoldstadt-2022.text: Stoppard's deeply personal Holocaust drama earns widespread acclaim as a haunting, emotionally devastating meditation on memory and Jewish identity, though some critics find its sprawling 38-member cast difficult to track across five decades.

cost-of-living-2022.text: Majok's Pulitzer-winning drama earns strong praise for its unsentimental exploration of caregivers and disability, anchored by exceptional performances. Critics laud its emotional depth and compassionate writing, though some find it occasionally cloying.

1776-2022.text: This diverse, all-female/trans/nonbinary revival of the 1969 musical earns mixed-to-positive reviews for its vibrant cast and bold reimagining, though some critics find the concept overshadows the material or feels heavy-handed in execution.

death-of-a-salesman-2022.text: Critics praise this historic revival with a Black Loman family, led by powerhouse performances from Wendell Pierce and Sharon D. Clarke that add new dimensions to Miller's classic, though some find the directorial choices distracting from the play's emotional core.

the-piano-lesson-2022.text: This starry revival of August Wilson's Pulitzer-winning drama earns praise for its powerful performances and reverent direction, though critics are divided on whether the production fully captures the play's emotional depth and tonal balance.

topdog-underdog-2022.text: Parks' Pulitzer-winning play crackles with vitality in this electrifying revival, powered by powerhouse performances from Hawkins and Abdul-Mateen II that bring fresh urgency to the intense two-hander about brotherhood and survival.

walking-with-ghosts-2022.text: Gabriel Byrne's storytelling gifts and charisma captivate, but this memoir adaptation divides critics who question whether the familiar material justifies its length and theatrical form, despite his undeniable stage presence.

almost-famous-2022.text: Critics are mixed on this rock musical adaptation, praising Casey Likes' performance and nostalgic energy but faulting lackluster songs, choppy storytelling, and failure to capture the film's magic or justify its stage existence.

kimberly-akimbo-2022.text: Critics hail this quirky musical as a refreshingly original triumph that balances hilarious comedy with heartbreaking poignancy. Victoria Clark's performance and the show's emotional depth earn widespread acclaim.

mike-birbiglia-the-old-man-and-the-pool-.text: Birbiglia's latest solo show earns strong praise for his masterful storytelling and ability to find humor in mortality and aging, though some critics note he's sticking to his familiar formula rather than breaking new ground.

a-christmas-carol-2022.text: Jefferson Mays dazzles in a technically ambitious one-man "Christmas Carol," though critics split on whether the dark, effects-heavy staging enhances or overshadows Dickens' timeless tale of redemption.

kpop-2022.text: Critics find KPOP visually spectacular with electrifying performances and choreography, but fault its thin plot and weak dramaturgy. The show's transition from immersive off-Broadway hit to traditional Broadway musical lost much of its original impact.

aint-no-mo-2022.text: Critics mostly praise Cooper's audacious satire as wildly funny and uncompromising, with comparisons to "The Colored Museum." However, many note the sketch comedy is uneven, swinging between brilliant moments and heavy-handed messaging.

ohio-state-murders-2022.text: Critics praise Audra McDonald's mesmerizing, powerfully controlled performance in Adrienne Kennedy's belated Broadway debut, though some find the brief, restrained production more reverential than fully alive as theater.

some-like-it-hot-2022.text: Critics largely embrace this energetic adaptation as a razzle-dazzle crowd-pleaser with spectacular choreography and modern sensibilities, though some find the score derivative and the contemporary updates heavy-handed.

the-collaboration-2022.text: Critics find Bettany and Pope magnetic as Warhol and Basquiat, but the play itself disappoints, offering a surface-level, Wikipedia-like treatment that lacks dramatic tension and fresh insights into the artists' collaboration.

between-riverside-and-crazy-2022.text: Henderson delivers a powerhouse performance in Guirgis's Pulitzer-winning comedy-drama, which critics praise for its vibrant dialogue and compelling ensemble, though some find the plot meanders. A streetwise New York story that balances humor with social commentary.

pictures-from-home-2023.text: Critics find this adaptation of Larry Sultan's photo memoir elevated by three stellar performances from Lane, Burstein, and Wanamaker, but hampered by a thin, repetitive script that leans on shtick and sentiment over substance.

a-dolls-house-2023.text: Critics are divided on Jamie Lloyd's ultra-minimalist revival: Chastain's performance earns widespread praise, but the stripped-down staging proves polarizing—some find it hypnotic and focused, others consider it lifeless.

parade-2023.text: This timely revival of Jason Robert Brown's dark musical earns acclaim for its urgent relevance and powerhouse performances from Ben Platt and Micaela Diamond, though some find the material heavy-handed despite its gorgeous score.

bob-fosses-dancin-2023.text: Critics find this revival thrilling to watch but dramatically hollow, praising the formidable dancers' athleticism and energy while noting the show lacks narrative drive and feels more like a stylish museum piece than vital theater.

bad-cinderella-2023.text: Lloyd Webber's fairy tale update receives largely negative reviews, criticized as confused, crass, and rudderless despite occasional campy fun. Critics fault its muddled tone and shallow feminist pretensions.

sweeney-todd-2023.text: Groban and Ashford lead a triumphant, full-scale revival that honors Sondheim's masterpiece with vocal power and theatrical ambition. Critics praise the lush orchestrations and performances, though some find the staging less daring than the material.

life-of-pi-2023.text: Critics praise *Life of Pi* for its stunning puppetry and visual spectacle, calling it a landmark in stagecraft. However, many find the emotional depth doesn't fully match the technical wizardry, with some noting the story feels secondary to the dazzling effects.

shucked-2023.text: Critics find "Shucked" an aggressively corny but surprisingly sweet musical comedy that delivers relentless puns and country-flavored charm. The jokes and catchy score mostly land, though some find the humor exhausting and the plot thin.

fat-ham-2023.text: Critics largely embrace this Pulitzer-winning Hamlet riff set at a Southern BBQ, praising its raucous humor and fresh take on masculinity and violence, though some find it more sketch-comedy than substantive drama.

camelot-2023.text: Sorkin's revision of Lerner and Loewe's classic divides critics: some appreciate the updated approach and gorgeous score, but many find his removal of magic elements leaves the show overly talky, lacking sparkle, and surprisingly dull.

peter-pan-goes-wrong-2023.text: Critics find this slapstick disaster-farce technically impressive and crowd-pleasing, with families and kids especially delighted, though some reviewers felt the repetitive physical comedy wore thin over two hours.

the-thanksgiving-play-2023.text: FastHorse's satire of performative wokeness earns laughs skewering well-meaning white liberals, but critics are divided on whether its 2015-era humor feels dated or still sharp, with some finding it hilarious and others saying it grazes rather than lands its targets.

prima-facie-2023.text: Jodie Comer delivers an extraordinary tour de force in her Broadway debut, commanding the stage solo for 100 minutes in this searing drama about sexual assault and the law, though some critics find Miller's play overly didactic.

good-night-oscar-2023.text: Hayes delivers a powerhouse performance as Oscar Levant in Wright's biographical play, though critics split on whether the exposition-heavy script does justice to its forgotten subject beyond the star's virtuosic acting and piano playing.

summer-1976-2023.text: Critics find Auburn's memory play a "pleasant wisp" elevated by powerhouse performances from Linney and Hecht, though most agree the quiet, nostalgic two-hander lacks dramatic heft and feels thin despite its exquisite acting.

new-york-new-york-2023.text: Critics find this Kander and Ebb musical a sprawling, unfocused love letter to NYC that prioritizes spectacle over substance. While Stroman's choreography dazzles and some performances shine, the show feels long-winded, overstuffed, and surprisingly dull.

the-sign-in-sidney-brusteins-window-2023.text: Isaac and Brosnahan lead a strong ensemble in Hansberry's sprawling, verbose play about 1960s Greenwich Village idealism. Critics are divided: some praise its ambition and relevance, others find it messy and overlong.

pass-over-2021.text: Critics praise this urgent, powerful drama as a bold Broadway reopening, blending Beckett and Exodus to examine Black lives with dark humor and intensity, though some question if its confrontational message will reach beyond the converted.

waitress-2021.text: Critics find *Waitress* a crowd-pleasing but safe musical elevated by Jessie Mueller's magnetic star turn and Sara Bareilles' appealing pop score, though some fault the overstuffed book and reliance on Broadway conventions.

lackawanna-blues-2021.text: Santiago-Hudson delivers a virtuosic performance in this warmhearted autobiographical solo show, expertly embodying dozens of characters from his 1950s boarding house childhood, though some critics find the memory play more self-indulgent than essential.

chicken-and-biscuits-2021.text: Critics find this family funeral comedy a mixed but mostly satisfying crowd-pleaser, with broad humor and warmth overcoming sitcom-style plotting and uneven tonal shifts that veer from laughter to sentimentality.

is-this-a-room-2021.text: Critics praise this verbatim FBI transcript as a gripping, pulse-pounding thriller that transforms a dry government document into taut, anxiety-inducing theater, though its 65-minute brevity leaves some wanting more.

thoughts-of-a-colored-man-2021.text: Critics find Keenan Scott II's exploration of Black masculinity ambitious and timely, praising the captivating seven-actor ensemble and blend of poetry and drama, though some note uneven execution and overly schematic moments.

the-lehman-trilogy-2021.text: Critics hail this epic as a theatrical triumph, praising Sam Mendes' direction and three extraordinary actors who bring 164 years of financial history to gripping life, though some find the 3+ hour spectacle soulless and historically blinkered.

dana-h-2021.text: Critics hail this experimental docudrama as mesmerizing and unforgettable, with Deirdre O'Connell's lip-synced performance of a harrowing abduction story earning near-universal praise as a stunning technical and emotional feat unlike anything on Broadway.

caroline-or-change-2021.text: Critics largely embrace this timely revival, praising Sharon D Clarke's towering performance and Tesori's eclectic score, though some find the show overlong and didactic. A prescient work finally getting its due recognition.

diana-the-musical-2021.text: Critics savage this Princess Diana musical as superficial, tone-deaf, and ghoulish, with terrible songs and cringeworthy lyrics. A few find it mesmerizing camp, but most call it exploitative schlock that reduces a tragic figure to tabloid fodder.

trouble-in-mind-2021.text: Childress's long-overdue Broadway debut arrives 65 years late but feels urgently relevant, with critics praising its prescient examination of racism in theater and LaChanze's commanding performance, though some find the production uneven.

clydes-2021.text: Lynn Nottage's heartfelt workplace comedy about ex-cons finding redemption in a truck stop sandwich shop earns warm reviews for its humor and strong performances, particularly Uzo Aduba, though some critics find it lighter than her Pulitzer-winning work.

slave-play-2021.text: Harris's provocative drama about race, sex, and interracial relationships divides critics: many praise its audacious exploration of difficult themes and strong performances, while others find it overwrought and dramatically messy.

company-2021.text: Elliott's gender-swapped revival earns mostly strong praise as a vital, brilliantly conceived reimagining that feels fresh and modern, though some critics find the central performance lacking and question whether the changes fully justify themselves.

flying-over-sunset-2021.text: Critics are divided on this LSD-themed musical about Cary Grant, Aldous Huxley, and Clare Boothe Luce. Many find it dull and overstuffed despite stunning visuals and Tony Yazbeck's spectacular dancing, comparing it to watching others' boring trips while sober.

skeleton-crew-2022.text: Morisseau's compassionate drama about Detroit auto workers facing plant closure earns praise for strong performances, especially Rashad's, and authentic atmosphere, though some critics find it stronger on character than plot.

the-music-man-2022.text: Critics are mixed on this starry revival, with Jackman and Foster's chemistry praised but many finding the production surprisingly flat and uninspired despite its big-budget polish and talented leads.

plaza-suite-2022.text: Critics find this Neil Simon revival a dated but crowd-pleasing star vehicle, with Parker and Broderick's charm and comic chemistry elevating material that feels increasingly old-fashioned 54 years later.

paradise-square-2022.text: Critics find Paradise Square an ambitious but overstuffed musical about Civil War-era New York, with Joaquina Kalukango's powerhouse performance and Bill T. Jones's thrilling choreography elevating a sprawling, unfocused book.

birthday-candles-2022.text: Critics find Birthday Candles a mixed bag, praising Messing's tour-de-force performance aging from 17 to 107, but faulting Haidle's play as manipulative, treacly, and overstuffed with life-affirming clichés that collapse under their own weight.

american-buffalo-2022.text: Mixed reviews greet this starry revival of Mamet's 1975 classic. Critics praise the powerhouse performances from Rockwell, Fishburne, and Criss, but many question whether the play's profane dialogue and themes feel dated or revelatory in 2022.

the-minutes-2022.text: Critics find Letts' dark political satire starts as a witty comedy about small-town council meetings before taking a disturbing turn into America's revisionist history, with strong ensemble performances elevating what some consider minor but timely work.

how-i-learned-to-drive-2022.text: Vogel's Pulitzer-winning play about grooming and abuse remains powerfully relevant 25 years later. Parker and Morse deliver incandescent performances in this emotionally complex, unsettling yet moving revival that critics largely praise as a modern masterpiece.

for-colored-girls-who-have-considered-su.text: Critics hail Camille A. Brown's "thrilling" and "exuberant" revival of Shange's choreopoem as a triumphant Broadway homecoming, praising its vibrant choreography and powerful performances, though a few find it lacking nuance.

hangmen-2022.text: McDonagh's pitch-black comedy about England's last hangman draws praise for its mordant wit and dark humor, though some critics find it overlong and derivative of Pinter. Strong performances elevate this menacing thriller with laughs.

funny-girl-2022.text: Critics are divided on this long-awaited revival: Beanie Feldstein's casting drew harsh criticism for lacking vocal power, but Lea Michele's later takeover earned widespread praise for finally delivering the star quality the role demands.

the-skin-of-our-teeth-2022.text: Blain-Cruz's visually spectacular production of Wilder's allegorical epic earns mixed reviews: critics praise the stunning design and ambitious scale, but many find the execution inconsistent, overlong, and chaotic despite its timely themes.

a-strange-loop-2022.text: Critics hail this Pulitzer-winning meta-musical as brazenly original and brutally honest, with many calling it revolutionary for Broadway. Its explicit exploration of Black queer identity proves electrifying, though some find it relentlessly raw.

mr-saturday-night-2022.text: Crystal shines with expert comic timing and old-school laughs, but critics find the musical adaptation overstuffed and forgettable, with a weak book and unmemorable songs that feel like unnecessary additions to what works best as pure stand-up.

macbeth-2022.text: Sam Gold's stripped-down "Macbeth" starring Daniel Craig and Ruth Negga divides critics with its unconventional staging choices. While the leads earn praise, the production is deemed puzzling and uneven, with gimmicky elements overshadowing Shakespeare's tragedy.

girl-from-the-north-country-2022.text: Critics praise McPherson's haunting Depression-era drama woven with Dylan's songs as a poetic, beautifully performed work that transcends the jukebox musical format, though some find it overstuffed with bleak clichés and slow pacing.

mrs-doubtfire-2021.text: Critics find this Broadway adaptation a pleasant but uninspired cash grab that fails to justify its existence beyond the film. Rob McClure's energetic performance earns praise, but the show relies on dated tropes and forgettable songs.

frankie-and-johnny-in-the-clair-de-lune-.text: McDonald and Shannon deliver powerhouse performances in this McNally revival, but critics are divided on whether the 1987 romantic two-hander's sexual politics have aged well, with some finding it dated and overlong despite its emotional resonance.

betrayal-2019.text: Jamie Lloyd's minimalist revival of Pinter's reverse-chronology infidelity drama earns strong praise for its spare, stylish staging and surgical precision from leads Tom Hiddleston, Charlie Cox, and Zawe Ashton, though some find it emotionally remote.

the-height-of-the-storm-2019.text: Pryce and Atkins deliver powerful performances in Zeller's puzzle-box drama about aging and dementia, though critics are divided on whether the playwright's familiar tricks illuminate or obscure the emotional core.

the-great-society-2019.text: Critics find this LBJ sequel overstuffed and less compelling than its predecessor, though Brian Cox delivers a powerful performance. The sprawling historical drama fascinates but struggles under the weight of too many events and characters.

linda-vista-2019.text: Letts' character study of a toxic middle-aged man draws mixed reactions—praised for sharp writing and Ian Barford's honest performance, but criticized for its nearly three-hour focus on an unlikable protagonist at a culturally tone-deaf moment.

the-rose-tattoo-2019.text: Mixed reviews for this Tennessee Williams revival, with critics divided on director Trip Cullman's broad comedic approach. Marisa Tomei earns praise for her committed performance, though many feel she's miscast and the production miscalibrates the play's tone.

the-lightning-thief-2019.text: Critics are mixed on this teen-targeted Greek mythology musical, finding it energetic but derivative. While some praise its charm and inventiveness, many cite thin substance, forgettable songs, and pale comparisons to Harry Potter.

the-sound-inside-2019.text: Critics praise Mary-Louise Parker's magnetic performance and Adam Rapp's literary writing in this dark two-hander, though some find it too cerebral and note Studio 54 is too large a venue for its intimate scale.

tina-2019.text: Adrienne Warren delivers an electrifying, powerhouse performance that transcends the show's formulaic jukebox-musical structure, earning near-universal praise for her vocal prowess and commanding stage presence in this by-the-book bio-musical.

the-inheritance-2019.text: Critics largely praise this ambitious, emotionally powerful 6+ hour epic about gay men grappling with AIDS legacy and generational divides, though some find it overlong and indulgent. Strong performances and moving moments outweigh structural flaws.

a-christmas-carol-2019.text: Jack Thorne's adaptation earns praise for its darker tone, social conscience, and immersive spectacle, though some critics find it favors style over substance. Campbell Scott's Scrooge and Jefferson Mays' virtuosic solo turn draw acclaim.

jagged-little-pill-2019.text: Critics find this Alanis Morissette jukebox musical ambitious but overstuffed, tackling numerous social issues with mixed results. Strong performances and effective song integration earn praise, though many feel the earnest, issue-heavy book strains under its own weight.

my-name-is-lucy-barton-2020.text: Critics are divided on this Laura Linney solo show adapted from Elizabeth Strout's novel. While Linney's luminous performance earns widespread praise, many find the 90-minute monologue underpowered, tedious, or lacking theatrical vitality despite its emotional depth.

a-soldiers-play-2020.text: Fuller's Pulitzer winner makes a powerful, long-overdue Broadway debut in Leon's riveting revival, with critics praising its enduring relevance and strong ensemble led by Grier and Underwood, though some find its conventional structure dated.

grand-horizons-2020.text: Wohl's sitcom-style boulevard comedy about a long-married couple's late-life split draws mixed reviews. Critics praise Alexander and Cromwell's performances but find the play familiar and uneven in balancing humor with depth.

west-side-story-2020.text: Ivo van Hove's radical reimagining divides critics with its video-heavy staging and elimination of iconic Robbins choreography. While some praise its bold, visceral modernization, others find it a muddled, gimmicky mess that overshadows the musical's heart.

the-boys-in-the-band-2018.text: This star-studded 50th anniversary revival proves Crowley's landmark 1968 play still packs emotional punch, despite feeling dated. Critics praise the stellar cast led by Parsons for balancing sharp wit with raw self-loathing.

straight-white-men-2018.text: Critics find Lee's groundbreaking play (first by an Asian-American woman on Broadway) smart and thought-provoking but dramatically uneven, with strong performances and humor undermined by unclear focus and unsatisfying resolution.

head-over-heels-2018.text: Critics are mixed on this Go-Go's/Elizabethan mash-up, with many praising its LGBTQ inclusivity and energetic choreography but questioning whether the '80s pop hits and Renaissance pastoral truly mesh, calling it goofy fun that doesn't always work.

gettin-the-band-back-together-2018.text: Critics largely pan this original Jersey-set rock musical as formulaic and amateurish, though some find its dopey charm and enthusiastic cast grudgingly enjoyable despite the predictable plot and forgettable score.

pretty-woman-the-musical-2018.text: Critics find "Pretty Woman: The Musical" a middling, overly faithful film adaptation hampered by a bland Bryan Adams score and dated premise, though Samantha Barks earns praise for her charismatic performance in an otherwise uninspired production.

bernhardthamlet-2018.text: McTeer delivers a magnetic, tour-de-force performance as Sarah Bernhardt, but critics find Rebeck's play overwritten and dramatically uneven, with a strong first act that loses momentum in the second despite timely feminist themes.

the-nap-2018.text: Critics are divided on this British snooker comedy, with many praising Bean's witty dialogue and the game cast, while others find it sluggish and less funny than his previous hit, with inconsistent pacing and problematic accents.

the-lifespan-of-a-fact-2018.text: Critics find this journalism ethics debate engaging and timely, elevated by a stellar cast (Radcliffe, Jones, Cannavale), though many feel the 85-minute play remains somewhat shallow and undercooked despite its provocative premise.

the-ferryman-2018.text: Critics hail Butterworth's epic Irish family drama as a masterpiece, praising Mendes' direction and the superb ensemble cast. Though some find it overstuffed or heavy-handed, most celebrate its thrilling storytelling and emotional power across 3+ riveting hours.

the-waverly-gallery-2018.text: Elaine May delivers a masterful, heartbreaking performance in her Broadway return, anchoring Lonergan's poignant dementia drama. Critics praise the stellar cast and sensitive direction, though some find the memory play's structure occasionally distancing.

torch-song-2018.text: Critics largely praise Michael Urie's virtuoso performance in this trimmed revival of Fierstein's landmark gay play, finding it still relevant and deeply moving. Some feel the abridged version exposes narrative weaknesses and can't escape the original's shadow.

american-son-2018.text: Critics find this timely racial drama provocative and topical, with Kerry Washington delivering a riveting, powerhouse performance, though many fault the play's heavy-handed dialogue, melodramatic structure, and lack of subtlety.

king-kong-2018.text: The spectacular 2,000-pound Kong puppet awes with technical wizardry, but critics find the musical surrounding him disappointingly hollow, with forgettable songs and a lifeless book that can't match the artistry of its animatronic star.

the-new-one-2018.text: Critics warmly embrace Birbiglia's solo show about reluctant fatherhood, praising his ability to blend personal storytelling with universal humor and genuine emotion, though some find it occasionally grating or less impactful in its final stretch.

the-prom-2018.text: Critics largely embrace "The Prom" as a joyful, heartfelt crowd-pleaser with infectious energy and strong performances, though some find its satire of Broadway narcissism stronger than its earnest coming-out story, and a few dismiss it as shallow or overly broad.

the-cher-show-2018.text: Critics find "The Cher Show" a flashy, entertaining jukebox musical elevated by Stephanie J. Block's standout performance, though the shallow book and rushed storytelling prevent deeper engagement.

network-2018.text: Critics praise Bryan Cranston's powerhouse performance in this multimedia-heavy adaptation, but reactions split on Ivo van Hove's tech-saturated staging—some find it thrilling and timely, others feel the spectacle overwhelms the human drama and dated satire.

to-kill-a-mockingbird-2018.text: Sorkin's adaptation earns mostly positive reviews for its strong performances and contemporary relevance, though some critics fault it for overwriting and shifting focus from Scout's perspective to white guilt themes.

choir-boy-2019.text: Critics praise Jeremy Pope's star-making performance and the gorgeous gospel singing in McCraney's coming-of-age drama, though some find the plot thin and overly familiar. The play's exploration of a gay Black teen at prep school resonates despite structural issues.

true-west-2019.text: Critics are divided on this revival of Shepard's classic, with praise for Hawke's menacing performance but concerns about uneven chemistry between the leads and a production that doesn't fully capture the play's raw power.

be-more-chill-2019.text: Critics are divided on this viral hit's Broadway transfer: younger audiences embrace its energetic pop-rock score and sci-fi high school story, but many reviewers find it frenetic, overwrought, and reliant on tired teen tropes despite a game cast.

kiss-me-kate-2019.text: O'Hara's luminous performance and Carlyle's dazzling choreography enliven this handsome revival, though Ellis's direction lacks spark and the show's dated gender politics prove difficult to fully overcome despite well-intentioned tweaks.

aint-too-proud-2019.text: Critics find this Temptations jukebox musical elevated by stellar performances and irresistible music, but hampered by conventional storytelling and shallow drama that rarely digs beneath the surface.

what-the-constitution-means-to-me-2019.text: Critics hail Schreck's genre-defying civics lesson as timely, funny, and deeply moving, praising its ingenious blend of personal memoir and constitutional debate. A few find it overly lecture-like, but most consider it essential, emotionally powerful theater.

king-lear-2019.text: Jackson delivers a formidable, commanding performance at 82, but Sam Gold's cluttered, uneven direction undermines the production with distracting gimmicks and inconsistent staging choices.

oklahoma-2019.text: Critics largely praise Daniel Fish's bold, stripped-down revival for excavating the darkness beneath the classic's sunny surface, with standout performances and bluegrass orchestrations earning acclaim, though some traditionalists find the reimagining pretentious or gimmicky.

burn-this-2019.text: Adam Driver delivers an explosive, tour-de-force performance that dominates this uneven revival, but he and Keri Russell lack the essential chemistry to ignite Wilson's dated 1987 drama, which feels increasingly out of step with contemporary sensibilities.

hillary-and-clinton-2019.text: Metcalf and Lithgow deliver strong performances in this speculative 2008-set drama, but critics find Hnath's play smart yet slight, offering witty dialogue without fresh insights into the Clintons' marriage or politics.

gary-a-sequel-to-titus-andronicus-2019.text: Critics are divided on Taylor Mac's audacious, blood-soaked comedy starring Nathan Lane. While some praise its wild originality and philosophical ambition, others find it an uneven, overlong mess that wastes its stellar cast on crude humor and muddled messaging.

all-my-sons-2019.text: Miller's postwar drama receives a powerful, traditional revival anchored by stellar performances from Bening and Letts, though some critics find the production's straightforward approach can't fully overcome the play's heavy-handed structure.

tootsie-2019.text: Critics praise "Tootsie" as a hilarious, crowd-pleasing musical comedy with a razor-sharp book by Robert Horn and standout performance by Santino Fontana, though many find David Yazbek's score forgettable and question its handling of gender politics.

ink-2019.text: Critics praise Graham's energetic, well-crafted drama about Murdoch's tabloid revolution, with standout performances from Miller and Carvel and Goold's flashy direction, though some find it overlong and lacking deeper character exploration.

beetlejuice-2019.text: Critics are split on this manic musical adaptation: fans praise Brightman's energetic performance and eye-popping visuals, while detractors find it exhaustingly loud with a forgettable score and crude humor that misses the film's charm.

1984-2017.text: Critics find this visceral adaptation of Orwell's dystopian classic timely and intensely harrowing, though some question whether its relentless sensory assault overshadows the story's deeper message.

the-terms-of-my-surrender-2017.text: Moore's anti-Trump Broadway debut earns mixed reviews as an entertaining but self-indulgent political rally. Critics praise his charm and storytelling skills, though many note it's more pep talk than theater, preaching to the choir with occasional laughs and inspiration.

prince-of-broadway-2017.text: A talented cast delivers strong performances of beloved Broadway songs, but this career retrospective lacks depth and cohesion. The show entertains musical theater fans with nostalgic highlights while offering little insight into Prince himself.

time-and-the-conways-2017.text: This handsomely staged revival of Priestley's 1937 drama earns praise for its design and ensemble performances, but critics find the dated drawing-room piece more intriguing as concept than compelling drama.

m-butterfly-2017.text: Mixed-to-negative reviews for Taymor's revival of Hwang's Tony-winner. Critics find the updated production cerebral but emotionally flat, with striking visuals that can't compensate for missing chemistry and spark that made the 1988 original electrifying.

junk-2017.text: Akhtar's ambitious financial drama about '80s junk bonds draws mixed reviews. Critics praise its brisk pacing and relevance but fault its overstuffed cast, lack of sympathetic characters, and familiar territory that feels more like a lecture than lived drama.

the-bands-visit-2017.text: Critics hail this intimate, understated musical as a ravishing gem that defies Broadway conventions with its quiet beauty, exquisite Middle Eastern-inflused score, and deeply human storytelling about connection across cultures.

latin-history-for-morons-2017.text: Leguizamo delivers an energetic, politically urgent performance that's hilarious and educational, though critics note the show feels overlong and unfocused. His masterful mimicry and timely subject matter largely compensate for its scattershot structure.

meteor-shower-2017.text: Steve Martin's absurdist comedy draws mixed reviews, with critics praising the strong cast—especially Amy Schumer's Broadway debut—but finding the play feels like an overextended sketch that's more scattershot than substantial.

the-parisian-woman-2017.text: Uma Thurman's Broadway debut in this Trump-era political drama draws mixed reviews. Critics praise her star power and Blair Brown's supporting turn, but fault the play's shallow writing, stilted dialogue, and dated feel despite topical references.

once-on-this-island-2017.text: Michael Arden's immersive, inventive revival transforms this Caribbean fable into a joyful, timely celebration. Critics praise the exuberant staging, vibrant performances, and infectious score, though a few find it overstuffed or slight.

spongebob-squarepants-2017.text: Critics find this vibrant cartoon adaptation surprisingly entertaining, praising Ethan Slater's star-making performance and dazzling psychedelic design, though some note the eclectic score lacks cohesion and the show feels overstuffed.

the-children-2017.text: Critics praise Kirkwood's thought-provoking post-nuclear drama for its superb acting and philosophical depth, though some find the pacing slow. The transferred Royal Court production earns acclaim for its subtle direction and timely exploration of generational responsibility.

farinelli-and-the-king-2017.text: Rylance delivers a masterful, riveting performance as the mad Spanish king, elevating a thin, simplistic script. Glorious Handel arias and candlelit atmosphere enchant, though the plot proves wanly eventless for some critics.

john-lithgow-stories-by-heart-2018.text: Critics are charmed by Lithgow's masterful storytelling and warm presence, but many find the material too slight for Broadway, better suited to a more intimate venue. His personal anecdotes resonate more than the vintage stories themselves.

escape-to-margaritaville-2018.text: Critics find this Jimmy Buffett jukebox musical a lightweight, predictable diversion with a thin plot and cardboard characters, though the talented cast and breezy songs offer pleasant escapism for Parrotheads willing to check their brains at the door.

frozen-2018.text: Critics find "Frozen" a visually impressive but unimaginative adaptation that pleases fans while disappointing those seeking theatrical magic beyond the film. Strong performances, especially from the leads, can't overcome a padded story and forgettable new songs.

lobby-hero-2018.text: Critics praise this timely revival of Lonergan's smart, morally complex drama, with Brian Tyree Henry singled out as a standout in a strong ensemble cast. The play's themes of power, ethics, and accountability resonate powerfully, though some find the pacing uneven.

three-tall-women-2018.text: Critics hail this long-awaited Broadway premiere as a triumph, with Glenda Jackson delivering a towering, mesmerizing performance in her return after 30 years. Mantello's direction and the entire cast earn widespread praise for Albee's Pulitzer-winning masterwork.

mean-girls-2018.text: Critics find Mean Girls an energetic, visually dazzling adaptation with Fey's sharp wit intact, but most agree the forgettable score holds it back from greatness. The young cast earns praise for their performances.

children-of-a-lesser-god-2018.text: Mixed reviews greet this revival of Medoff's 1979 play, praised for groundbreaking accessibility and Ridloff's fierce performance but criticized for feeling dated, lacking chemistry, and Jackson's uneven work.

carousel-2018.text: Critics praise Joshua Henry's powerhouse performance and the glorious Rodgers & Hammerstein score, but this handsome revival struggles with the show's dated treatment of domestic abuse, yielding mixed results despite stellar singing and Justin Peck's thrilling choreography.

my-fair-lady-2018.text: Bartlett Sher's lavish Lincoln Center revival earns acclaim for its sumptuous production values, strong performances (especially Lauren Ambrose's Eliza), and a contemporary feminist twist on the ending, though some critics find it lacking urgency or a bold directorial vision.

summer-2018.text: Critics find this jukebox musical a formulaic, threadbare disappointment that fails to do justice to Donna Summer's legacy, though the show's three lead vocalists deliver strong performances and the iconic disco hits remain irresistible.

travesties-2018.text: Critics hail this "sparkling" and "exultant" revival of Stoppard's brainy 1974 comedy as a "giddy triumph," praising Marber's pitch-perfect direction and Hollander's brilliant performance, though some find the dense wordplay exhausting or impenetrable.

saint-joan-2018.text: Critics are mixed on this Shaw revival, praising Condola Rashad's luminous performance and strong supporting cast, but finding Daniel Sullivan's direction stolid and slow-paced, with the production struggling to ignite Shaw's verbose three-hour epic.

the-iceman-cometh-2018.text: Critics largely praise this energetic revival of O'Neill's epic, with Denzel Washington delivering a powerful performance as Hickey alongside a stellar ensemble cast, though some find his portrayal uneven and the production's brisk pace undercuts the play's darkness.

cirque-du-soleil-paramour-2016.text: Critics find Cirque du Soleil's Broadway debut visually stunning with impressive acrobatics, but hampered by a weak, generic storyline that awkwardly clashes with the spectacle rather than enhancing it.

an-act-of-god-2016.text: Critics find this comedy's irreverent premise more promising than its execution, with charismatic leads (Jim Parsons, later Sean Hayes) elevating uneven material that delivers sporadic laughs but lacks consistent inspiration.

motown-the-musical-2016.text: Critics find the Motown hits irresistible and performances energetic, but fault Berry Gordy's clunky, self-serving book for sanitizing history with clichéd dialogue and unfocused storytelling that merely connects beloved songs.

cats-2016.text: Critics remain divided on this Broadway revival, with many noting the show's polarizing nature persists. While the energetic cast and dancing earn praise, detractors find it dated and plotless, though Lloyd Webber's catchy score proves undeniably memorable.

the-encounter-2016.text: Critics are deeply divided on this technologically ambitious solo show: some hail McBurney's binaural sound design as a revolutionary theatrical experience, while others find the two-hour Amazon journey tedious despite its initial sonic wizardry.

holiday-inn-the-new-irving-berlin-musica.text: Critics find this old-fashioned Irving Berlin musical a pleasant, toe-tapping diversion with spectacular dancing and beloved songs, though the formulaic book and lack of depth keep it from being more than agreeable comfort food for the holiday season.

oh-hello-on-broadway-2016.text: Kroll and Mulaney's extended sketch about cranky Upper West Side geezers earns mostly positive notices for its absurdist humor and character work, though some critics find the premise thin for a full Broadway show.

heisenberg-2016.text: Critics praise Parker and Arndt's stellar performances in this minimalist two-hander, though opinions split on Stephens' slim plot. The chemistry captivates most, but some find the quirky romance unconvincing and the 80-minute runtime slight.

the-cherry-orchard-2016.text: This revival of Chekhov's classic receives largely negative reviews, with critics finding it disjointed, flat, and dramatically underdeveloped despite a strong cast led by Diane Lane.

the-front-page-2016.text: Critics find this star-studded revival of the 1928 comedy sluggish and overlong until Nathan Lane arrives midway through to electrify the production, though even his acclaimed performance can't fully compensate for the dated material and uneven pacing.

falsettos-2016.text: This revival of Finn and Lapine's groundbreaking AIDS-era musical earns widespread praise for its stellar cast and emotional power, though some find the first act uneven. Critics hail it as fresh, heartbreaking, and exhilarating 25 years later.

les-liaisons-dangereuses-2016.text: Mixed reviews for this Donmar Warehouse revival, with critics divided on the leads' chemistry. Janet McTeer widely praised for her commanding Marquise, but Liev Schreiber seen as miscast. Production deemed handsome yet lacking heat and danger.

natasha-pierre-and-the-great-comet-of-18.text: Critics hail this immersive Tolstoy adaptation as a thrilling, visually spectacular pop-opera with inventive staging that transforms the Imperial Theatre, though some find the eclectic score uneven and the first act overlong.

a-bronx-tale-the-musical-2016.text: Critics find this crowd-pleasing musical entertaining but derivative, with a too-familiar story that feels unnecessary. Alan Menken's score and strong performances earn praise, though the material lacks the edge of earlier versions.

dear-evan-hansen-2016.text: Critics embrace this emotionally powerful musical about teen isolation and social media, praising Ben Platt's extraordinary star-making performance and Pasek & Paul's mature score, though some find the ending too pat and question its ethical resolution.

in-transit-2016.text: Broadway's first a cappella musical earns praise for its talented cast and impressive vocal harmonies, but critics find the subway-set stories predictable and stereotypical, making for a pleasant yet lightweight experience.

the-present-2017.text: Critics are divided on this Chekhov adaptation, with Blanchett's magnetic performance drawing praise but the three-hour production deemed lethargic and uneven by many, though some find it dazzling and engaging.

jitney-2017.text: Critics hail this long-awaited Broadway debut of Wilson's Pittsburgh Cycle play as a triumphant ensemble piece featuring extraordinary performances and Santiago-Hudson's pitch-perfect direction that captures the musicality of Wilson's dialogue and the dignity of working-class liv

sunset-boulevard-2017.text: Critics praise the lead performances as tour-de-force turns, but find the stripped-down production oddly diminished around them, with mixed reactions to the staging choices and vocal inconsistencies.

sunday-in-the-park-with-george-2017.text: Critics praise this emotionally rich revival of Sondheim's masterpiece, with Gyllenhaal's surprisingly strong vocals and Ashford's luminous performance anchoring a production that emphasizes intimacy over spectacle, though some find the staging too sparse.

significant-other-2017.text: Critics largely embrace Harmon's bittersweet comedy about a lonely gay man watching friends marry, praising Gideon Glick's heartbreaking performance, though some find the protagonist too whiny and the premise overly familiar.

the-glass-menagerie-2017.text: Critics are divided on Sam Gold's stripped-down revival: some praise Sally Field's fierce Amanda and the bold minimalist approach, while others find the stark concept undermines Williams' lyricism.

come-from-away-2017.text: Critics praise this heartwarming 9/11 musical about Gander's hospitality as uplifting and entertaining, with strong ensemble work and infectious Celtic-folk score, though some find it overly sentimental and lacking memorable songs.

the-price-2017.text: Critics praise Danny DeVito's scene-stealing Broadway debut and strong performances from Shalhoub and Hecht in this solid revival of Miller's lesser-known family drama, though some find the play itself slow and uneven in tone.

miss-saigon-2017.text: Critics are divided on this spectacle-driven revival: fans praise its lush score, stunning production values, and Eva Noblezada's breakout performance, while detractors find it melodramatic, dated, and reliant on Orientalist stereotypes that haven't aged well.

sweat-2017.text: Nottage's timely drama about factory workers in Reading, PA earns widespread praise for its empathetic character work and strong ensemble, though some critics find it heavy on exposition and overly familiar in its depiction of working-class decline.

the-play-that-goes-wrong-2017.text: Critics are mostly charmed by this West End import's precisely executed slapstick chaos, though some find the broad farce exhausting. The physical comedy earns comparisons to "Noises Off" and generates reliable laughs.

amelie-a-new-musical-2017.text: Critics find this whimsical adaptation struggles to capture the film's magic, with a workmanlike score and forced charm that exhausts more than enchants, though David Zinn's inventive Parisian set design wins praise.

present-laughter-2017.text: Kevin Kline delivers a masterful, physically comic performance in this stylish Coward revival, though some critics find the 1939 drawing-room comedy creaky and overlong. The production charms more than it thrills.

war-paint-2017.text: LuPone and Ebersole deliver powerhouse performances as cosmetics rivals Rubinstein and Arden, but critics find the show itself only skin-deep, with a forgettable score and overstuffed book that never fully captures what drove these pioneering businesswomen.

oslo-2017.text: Critics hail this political thriller as gripping and riveting despite its three-hour runtime, praising Rogers' ambitious script and Sher's fluid direction. The ensemble cast earns acclaim, though some find it talky and overlong. A compelling look at idealism and diplomacy.

groundhog-day-2017.text: Critics largely praise Andy Karl's charismatic, tour-de-force performance and Tim Minchin's inventive staging, though some find the show overlong and the score unmemorable. A clever, witty adaptation that mostly succeeds despite repetition concerns.

indecent-2017.text: Critics praise Paula Vogel's moving, theatrically inventive play about a controversial Yiddish drama, lauding Rebecca Taichman's stunning direction and the exceptional ensemble cast.

the-little-foxes-2017.text: Linney and Nixon's role-swapping anchors a superb revival of Hellman's Southern melodrama, with critics praising Sullivan's assured direction and the stellar ensemble cast in this timely tale of greed and family betrayal.

hello-dolly-2017.text: Critics hail this lavish revival as old-fashioned Broadway bliss, with Bette Midler earning raves for her commanding star turn, though some find her voice limited. Bernadette Peters wins equal praise for bringing warmth and vocal power to the role.

charlie-and-the-chocolate-factory-2017.text: Critics are sharply divided on this Broadway adaptation, with most finding it a disappointing, overstuffed spectacle lacking imagination despite Christian Borle's charismatic Wonka and some inventive second-act staging.

anastasia-2017.text: Critics find "Anastasia" a lavishly designed but uneven throwback musical that struggles with identity issues of its own. While praised for gorgeous visuals and nostalgic charm, many cite a thin book and overlong runtime that doesn't match the animated film's magic.

six-degrees-of-separation-2017.text: Critics praise Janney's commanding performance and Guare's sharp social satire, though some find Cullman's direction too broad and the 1990 play dated in the smartphone era. The revival earns respect but lacks the original's bite.

bandstand-2017.text: Critics praise Blankenbuehler's inventive choreography and the talented cast, but find this WWII veteran musical tonally uneven—struggling to balance swing-era entertainment with darker PTSD themes, hampered by a forgettable score and overly familiar book.

a-dolls-house-part-2-2017.text: Hnath's audacious sequel earns strong praise for its sharp, witty writing and thought-provoking feminist themes, with Metcalf's commanding performance leading an excellent cast.

amazing-grace-2015.text: Critics find "Amazing Grace" well-intentioned but dramatically uneven, with a stirring title hymn finale that can't redeem forgettable songs and a protagonist whose rushed redemption fails to convince. Strong performances and spectacle can't overcome the choppy storytelling.

spring-awakening-2015.text: Deaf West's innovative revival electrifies the 2006 Tony winner by integrating American Sign Language, with critics praising its theatrical power and accessibility despite some questioning the timing of a return just seven years after closing.

old-times-2015.text: Critics are divided on this stylish Pinter revival: strong performances from Owen, Best, and Reilly generate heat and intrigue, but Hodge's flashy direction—with Thom Yorke music and bold design—often overwhelms the play's intimate menace.

fool-for-love-2015.text: Critics are divided on this Shepard revival: Rockwell and Arianda deliver fierce, committed performances in a visceral production, but many find the 75-minute play feels dated, uninvolving, or too small for Broadway's larger stage.

the-gin-game-2015.text: Critics praise James Earl Jones and Cicely Tyson's masterful performances in this revival, finding the legendary duo's chemistry captivating despite the play's slim material and unsatisfying ending.

dames-at-sea-2015.text: Critics are divided on this featherweight spoof of 1930s movie musicals, with many questioning its Broadway viability. While the cast's tap-dancing dazzles, the dated material feels uncomfortably out of place despite charming moments.

sylvia-2015.text: Ashford's winning performance as the titular canine delights in this charming but lightweight Gurney comedy. Critics praise her physical comedy and comic timing, though most find the play itself thin and dated.

therese-raquin-2015.text: This uneven revival of Zola's melodrama earns mixed reviews, with critics praising the stunning production design but finding the slow-moving adaptation lifeless despite Knightley's committed Broadway debut.

king-charles-iii-2015.text: Bartlett's audacious "future history play" earns widespread praise for its clever Shakespearean verse and Tim Pigott-Smith's commanding performance, though some find the premise more intriguing for British audiences than Americans.

on-your-feet-2015.text: Critics find this Gloria Estefan biomusical formulaic but crowd-pleasing, with infectious Latin music and energetic performances overcoming a weak, TV-movie-style book. The rhythm gets you eventually.

allegiance-2015.text: Critics find "Allegiance" a well-intentioned but flawed musical about Japanese internment. While the cast (especially George Takei and Lea Salonga) earns praise and the subject matter resonates, the score and book are deemed generic and overly sentimental.

a-view-from-the-bridge-2015.text: Ivo van Hove's stripped-down, minimalist production earns widespread acclaim for its visceral intensity and Mark Strong's powerful performance, though some critics find the stark, experimental staging overly austere and less effective than traditional approaches.

misery-2015.text: Mixed reviews for this Broadway thriller: Laurie Metcalf earns praise for her chilling performance as deranged fan Annie Wilkes, but Bruce Willis disappoints in a flat, disengaged debut. The production lacks suspense and tension despite strong technical

china-doll-2015.text: Mamet's rambling, underdeveloped play wastes Pacino's star power on an incoherent two-hour phone monologue that critics found tedious and dramatically inert, despite occasional flashes of the playwright's signature dialogue.

school-of-rock-the-musical-2015.text: Lloyd Webber's high-energy adaptation delivers feel-good fun powered by talented kid performers, though the score lacks memorable songs and the formulaic book plays it safe.

the-color-purple-2015.text: John Doyle's stripped-down revival transforms "The Color Purple" into a triumph, with critics praising Cynthia Erivo's star-making performance and the minimalist staging that sharpens emotional impact, though some find the source material remains schematic.

fiddler-on-the-roof-2015.text: Bartlett Sher's revival earns strong praise for its fresh, emotionally resonant approach and Danny Burstein's deeply human Tevye, though some critics find it too subdued. The production's timely refugee themes and stripped-down staging mostly succeed.

noises-off-2016.text: Critics praise this precision-crafted revival as hilariously funny, with stellar comic performances (especially Megan Hilty) and expert direction. Some find it overfamiliar or note a weaker third act, but most agree it delivers sustained laughter.

our-mothers-brief-affair-2016.text: Linda Lavin's stellar performance elevates Greenberg's underwhelming drama about a mother's deathbed confession. Critics find the play unfocused and dramatically inert, though Lavin's wit and skill earn consistent praise.
